findings.title: IR13C uses the no-exposure canonical projection for its exposed ROLLED_BACK branch
findings.requirement: Every synchronized tuple row must stutter or traverse only the exact legal §2 canonical adjacency from the reducer-selected pre-state.
evidence: docs/state-transition-manifests.md §15.1 priority 7a says a no-cancellation WIDENING_ABORT with rollback ROLLED_BACK and cleanup NOT_REQUIRED remains canonical ROLLED_BACK through IR12/IR13A until IR13C schedules cleanup.
IR13A reaches CANARY_ABORT_SETTLED only with rollback exactly ROLLED_BACK, whereas IR13B is the no-exposure/rollback-IDLE branch.
IR13C combines both branch receipts but declares only `REVIEW>CLEANING`; REVIEW is the IR13B pre-state, not the IR13A pre-state. §2 provides `ROLLED_BACK>CLEANING` for the exposed branch.
findings.impact: A literal reducer rejects IR13C after a valid exposed canary abort, or an implementation ignores the stated projection. The sole WIDENING_ABORT/NONE cleanup path can strand after genuine rollback.
findings.required_correction: Split IR13C into exposed and no-exposure rows, or state a branch-dependent exact projection: `ROLLED_BACK>CLEANING` for IR13A and `REVIEW>CLEANING` for IR13B. Preserve the one-owner origin/cancellation partition and update exact witnesses.

findings.title: IC32 revocation totality omits reachable rollout FAILED and RETIRED cleanup tuples
findings.requirement: Candidate revocation must be total over the actual generated reachable rollout/effect/rollback/cancellation coordinates, with exact equality rather than a hand-maintained subset.
evidence: IR16 and related denial/withdrawal rows can move rollout to FAILED and schedule cleanup while candidate remains SHADOW_PASSED; before cleanup receipts finish, the tuple is reachable and nonterminal.
IR21 can move rollout OBSERVING->RETIRED and schedule cleanup while candidate remains SHADOW_PASSED; the tuple is nonterminal until cleanup completes.
The IC32 reachable-rollout declaration and IC32 row union omit FAILED and RETIRED, and no row adopts/stutters a later revocation without duplicating cleanup.
findings.impact: A revocation arriving during failure/retirement cleanup has no exact candidate transition despite the claimed generated equality and PLAN’s exact-rollout revocation contract. Authority/history handling is undefined at a reachable nonterminal coordinate.
findings.required_correction: Add exact cleanup-adoption revocation rows for reachable FAILED/RETIRED tuples that preserve the existing CleanupManifest and create no rollback/duplicate owner, or add a normative irreversible-disposition rule that safely rejects and records such events and removes those coordinates from the declared revocation domain. Regenerate equality witnesses from the actual fixed point.

findings.title: BUILD and MAINTENANCE post-remediation cancellation and cleanup rows overlap
findings.requirement: After rollback remediation, persisted cancellation must select exactly one continuation and cannot race ordinary failure cleanup.
evidence: B75 and M63 persist authenticated cancellation while remaining in ROLLBACK_REMEDIATION_WAIT.
After B74/M62, B34/B38 and M25/M29 can reach ROLLED_BACK with that cancellation disposition still persisted.

At ROLLED_BACK, B39/M30 require only an outcome receipt, while B71/M59 require authenticated cancellation after rollback settled. The ordinary rows do not require absence of cancellation, so both continuations are enabled.
findings.impact: The private BUILD/MAINTENANCE machines are nondeterministic at a safety-sensitive point. One scheduler can enter ordinary failure cleanup while another enters cancellation handling, undermining exact replay and sole cleanup/terminal ownership.
findings.required_correction: Partition the rows explicitly: B39/M30 require no persisted cancellation, and B71/M59 require the persisted cancellation disposition. Define CAS/replay behavior and add cancellation-during-remediation witnesses through ROLLED_BACK, cleanup, and CANCELLED.
